title: fix(sprite.ts): mask/masked layers in symbol timelines not clipped — HasClipDepth never emitted in DefineSprite
description:
sprite.ts encodeDefineSprite does not handle mask and masked layer types. compile.ts has a full mask/clipDepth handling section (lines 1346-1630) that:
- Identifies mask layers and their consecutive 'masked' children
- Assigns depths so the mask gets a LOWER depth than its masked layers (SWF requirement: mask at depth D clips D+1..clipDepth)
- Emits PlaceObject2 with HasClipDepth (and correct clipDepth value) for mask layers
- In the posChanged/move path also re-emits HasClipDepth to preserve clipping across movement

sprite.ts has NONE of this. When a symbol imported from a Flash 8 FLA has mask/masked layers (which flash8-import.ts correctly preserves via resolveMaskedLayers for symbol timelines), the mask layer's objects are placed as normal visible content and the masked layers are also placed normally -- no clipping occurs in Ruffle.

Affected file: packages/swf/src/sprite.ts

Fix prescription:
1. Before the pre-pass depth-seed loop (line 196), identify which layer indices are mask layers and which are masked layers (same analysis as compile.ts lines 1353-1397).
2. In the pre-pass, seed depths: process mask layers BEFORE their masked children to get lower depth values (same as compile.ts lines 1346-1399).
3. In the frame loop (line 230+), skip masked layers as they are iterated independently after their owning mask. After placing a mask layer's objects, compute clipDepth = max depth among consecutive masked layers below.
4. For mask layer objects, use encodePlaceObject2WithClipDepth (already imported in compile.ts; import it in sprite.ts too) instead of PlaceObject2.

Acceptance: a unit test in packages/swf/src/__tests__/ that creates a 2-frame symbol with a mask layer (red rect) and a masked layer (blue rect), compiles it via encodeDefineSprite, and asserts that the PlaceObject2 tag for the mask object has HasClipDepth set (and the correct clipDepth value pointing to the masked layer depth).
